key_concept: In the Arrhenius plot, $\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$, so the y-intercept of $\ln k$ vs $1/T$ gives $\ln A$ and the slope is $-E_a/R$.
steps: Write the linear form of the Arrhenius equation: $\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{R}\cdot\dfrac{1}{T}$.
From the graph, the line meets the $\ln k$ axis at 6, so $\ln A = 6$.
For $k = e^2\ \text{min}^{-1}$, $\ln k = 2$. Substituting gives $2 = 6 - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$, so $\dfrac{E_a}{RT} = 4$.
why_not_others: $125$ K or $150$ K follow from using a wrong intercept or a wrong $\ln k$ difference (for example $E_a/RT = 6$ or $2$ instead of $4$). $250$ K results from arithmetic slips such as dividing by $3.2R$.
common_trap: Students forget to convert $E_a$ from kJ to J ($6.64$ kJ $= 6640$ J), or they take $\ln k = e^2$ instead of $\ln k = 2$.
time_saving_tip: Read $\ln A$ directly from the intercept. Then $T = E_a / [R(\ln A - \ln k)]$, which here is $6640/(8.3 \times 4) = 200$ K in one line.
